Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.

body:
# Performance: measured, one real inefficiency found

Benchmarked `CompositeList` directly in headless Chromium (1000 items, `flushSync` mount/update, median of 12 rounds), on this PR's head vs `master`:

| Scenario (1000 items) | master | PR #5148 | PR + guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mount, uncontrolled | 26.0 ms | 26.7 ms | **6.4 ms** |
| Mount, controlled (`index` prop) | 4.8 ms † | 23.6 ms | **4.1 ms** |
| Replace half the items, uncontrolled | 47.0 ms | 47.6 ms | **26.6 ms** |
| Replace half the items, controlled | 4.6 ms † | 47.6 ms | **5.6 ms** |
| Filter 1000→500, controlled (all indexes reassigned) | 2.4 ms † | 36.6 ms | **3.3 ms** |
| Filter 1000→500, uncontrolled | 23.7 ms | 24.5 ms | **12.3 ms** |

† master's controlled numbers are the skip-registration path — fast because it did nothing, which is exactly the bug being fixed.

Reading the middle column: the PR is **perf-neutral for uncontrolled lists** (the common case), but large controlled lists pay real new cost — a filter keystroke on a 1000-item indexed Combobox costs ~34 ms more than master, per keystroke.

**The cost is not the sort — it's the state-update enqueue.** Both `register` and `unregister` call `setMapTick` once per item, so a 1000-item commit enqueues 1000 updates that React coalesces into one render anyway. Guarding the enqueue on the dirty-flag transition eliminates it:

```tsx
map.set(node, metadata);
if (!isDirtyRef.current) {
  isDirtyRef.current = true;
  setMapTick((tick) => tick + 1);
}
```

(and the same in `unregister`). This is safe by construction: every false→true dirty transition enqueues exactly one tick, and the only thing that clears the flag is `flush()`, which is guaranteed to run afterwards — either in the same commit's parent layout effect or in the tick-triggered render. With this guard, **all 2679 tests across the eleven affected suites pass**, and every scenario becomes faster than master — including the previously "free" controlled paths (4.1 vs 4.8 ms mount) and a 4× improvement on uncontrolled mounts, since master paid the same per-register enqueue tax.

# Minimality assessment

The architecture is close to minimal for what it has to preserve — I looked for structural cuts and found none that survive scrutiny: the `mapTick` state is the only mechanism that gets `CompositeList` to re-run its flush effect after child registrations (a dep-less effect wouldn't fire without a re-render); `sortedMapRef` is needed so late subscribers and the MutationObserver path get a current snapshot without a render; `isDirtyRef` is what lets one flush serve n registrations. The head commit already removed the redundant tick from `flush`. Remaining trims are cosmetic:

- `sortMap`'s controlled comparator `(a[1]?.index ?? 0)` — metadata can no longer be `null`/`undefined` in the map (the type changed in this PR), so the optional chaining and fallback are dead defensiveness.
- The `ComboboxItem` virtualized manual `listRef` effect now overlaps with registration-driven `syncRefs` for items that pass `index` (both write the same node into the same slot; the registration flush runs after the manual write in the same commit) — consolidating to a single writer is the one real simplification available.

The single actionable outcome of this pass is the `setMapTick` guard: a two-site, behavior-preserving change that turns the PR's only measurable regression into an across-the-board win over master.

---

🤖 Review generated with Claude Code

# Second pass: virtualized regressions

Follow-up hunt on the current head — the earlier findings (deep-subtree registration, per-register tick cost, `label: null`, vacuous warning tests) are all resolved now. This pass focused on the newly-changed virtualized path, since removing the `if (virtualized) return element` early-return means virtualized lists mount a `CompositeList` for the first time. Found one merge-blocking regression there plus a few smaller things.

## 1. 🔴 Virtualized: `listRef.current.length` is truncated to the rendered window, breaking keyboard bounds

On master, virtualized mode renders no `CompositeList`; items write `store.state.listRef.current[index] = el` directly (and `delete` on cleanup never shrinks `length`), while `AriaCombobox` maintains the invariant `listRef.current.length = flatFilteredItems.length` in a layout effect keyed on `[items, flatFilteredItems]`.

With this PR, every flush runs `syncRefs`, which does `elementsRef.current = []` and sparse-fills only the currently rendered window — the array is **replaced** with one whose `length` is `maxRenderedIndex + 1`, not the filtered total. The `AriaCombobox` fixup effect doesn't re-run (its deps haven't changed), and even when it does run in the same commit, the next window shift (scroll or key-repeat arrowing → items re-register with a new `index` → flush in the tick-triggered render) clobbers it again with no counter-fixup.

`useListNavigation` computes bounds from that length on every keydown (`getMaxListIndex` → `length - 1`; the combobox passes `disabledIndices: EMPTY_ARRAY`, so holes aren't skipped):

- `loopFocus` (default `true`) + `allowEscape` (true whenever `autoHighlight` is off): at `currentIndex >= maxIndex` the highlight **escapes to `-1` in the middle of the list** — reachable with key-repeat ArrowDown, which outruns the virtualizer's scroll-triggered re-window.
- With `autoHighlight` (no escape): **wraps to the top mid-list** instead of advancing.
- Trigger-based (non-typeable) virtualized combobox: **`End` jumps to the last *rendered* item**, not the last filtered item.

The new test `registers items at their filtered indexes when the rendered window starts after index 0` actually asserts the broken invariant: snapshot `'||three|four'` is length 4 while `flatFilteredItems.length` is 5 — pre-PR that snapshot would be `'||three|four|'`. JSDOM tests can't see the fallout because they don't exercise virtualizer window shifts.

**Fix direction:** either `syncRefs` shouldn't shrink/replace the array for controlled lists (mutate in place, never reduce `length`, leaving total-length ownership with `AriaCombobox`), or `ComboboxList` should re-assert `listRef.current.length = flatFilteredItems.length` after each flush (it already has `filteredItems` in scope and could pass an `onMapChange`).

## 2. 🟡 Virtualized items missing from the filter register with controlled index `-1`

`ComboboxItem.tsx`:

```ts
const index = indexProp ?? (virtualized ? (indexFromFilter ?? -1) : undefined);
```

`findItemIndex` returns `-1` (never `undefined`) when a rendered item isn't in `flatFilteredItems` — a normal transient state while a virtualizer's window lags a keystroke, so the `?? -1` arm is dead and `-1` flows through as a *controlled* index. On master these items were excluded (`hasRegistered` gated the manual write). Now they land in the sorted map (sorted first), and `syncRefs` executes `elementsRef.current[-1] = node` / `labelsRef.current[-1] = …` — junk string-keyed properties holding node references. If a whole stale window misses the filter, that flush produces an essentially empty `listRef` (length 0) for the commit — which also feeds regression 1. A `metadata.index >= 0` guard in `syncRefs` (or skipping registration of `-1` at the call site) closes it.

## 3. 🟡 MutationObserver is never re-created after an observer-triggered flush (uncontrolled lists)

On master, the MO callback called `setMapTick` → re-render → new `sortedMap` → the observer effect re-ran and re-observed the current parents. Now the MO callback calls `flush()` directly, which updates `sortedMapRef` but never bumps `mapTick`, and the observer effect only re-runs on `mapTick`. After a reorder that moves a node to a *different* parent (DnD libraries, manual DOM re-parenting — exactly the no-React-commit scenario this observer exists for), the new parent is never observed, so subsequent reorders under it go undetected until an unrelated register/unregister. Edge-case, but a strict capability loss vs master's re-observe-every-flush.

## 4. ℹ️ Stale type on `subscribeMapChange`

`CompositeListContextValue.subscribeMapChange` is still typed `(map: Map<Element, Metadata | null>) => void`, but listeners now always receive `Map<Element, CompositeMetadata<Metadata>>` — values are never `null` after this PR, and `index`/`labelRef` are what the subscriber in `useCompositeListItem` actually reads. Cosmetic, but it hides type errors in listener code.

## Checked and clear

- **Flush timing** (refs filled in `CompositeList`'s layout effect instead of item ref callbacks): every descendant reader checks out — `SelectPopup`'s `listRef.current[0]` read waits on `isPositioned` (a post-flush commit), `useCompositeRoot.onMapChange` runs inside the flush, and event handlers run long after.
- **`onMapChange` consumers** (Tabs, Toolbar, Slider, OTPField, SelectPositioner): all size-guarded or idempotent against the new call pattern (no more initial empty-map call; unregister-to-empty still flushes).
- **Mode transitions:** `controlledRef` resets correctly when the map empties (cleanups run before creates within a commit), and StrictMode double-invoke is safe.
- **Label semantics:** `label={null}` typeahead-exclusion survives, and label-change-without-reregister works via the `labelRef` indirection.
- **Registration churn:** the register effect's deps (`metadata`, `externalIndex`) have the same identity requirements as master — no new infinite-render risk.

No. 1 is the one I'd block on — it likely decides what `syncRefs`'s ownership contract over `elementsRef` should be.

# PR review

The core redesign is sound: registration-time flush ordering is correct (child layout effects registering before the parent's `flush`), the coalesced `isDirtyRef`/`mapTick` mechanism cannot miss a flush, and the wholesale `syncRefs` rebuild fixes real staleness the old optimistic ref-callback writes had. Nothing is merge-blocking; the findings below are robustness gaps at the edges of the new controlled mode.

## Bugs (3)

### 1. 🟡 Indexing mode is locked forever, so a legitimate full remount into the other mode silently breaks in production

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:21`

```tsx
// Whether item indexes are controlled (`index` props) or derived from DOM order. The mode is
// intentionally fixed to the first registered item and never reset so that during development
// any runtime mode switch surfaces an uncontrolled/controlled mixing error.
const controlledRef = React.useRef<boolean | null>(null);
```

The lock is intentional for catching *mixing*, but it also covers the non-mixing case where one item population fully unregisters and a new population registers in the opposite mode (e.g. a consumer that passes `index` only under some condition, without remounting the list). Once locked `controlled`, later uncontrolled registrations have `metadata.index === undefined`, so `sortMap`'s controlled branch never assigns indexes and `syncRefs` skips every item — `elementsRef`/`labelsRef` stay empty, keyboard navigation, hover highlighting, and typeahead all go dead. In the old code this swap worked (index-less items simply registered in DOM-order mode). In development you get one warning (and `error()` dedupes by its static message, so only the first offending list in a session logs it); in production the list is silently inert.

**Failure scenario:** An app renders `<Combobox.Item index={i}>` for a large dataset and plain `<Combobox.Item>` when a smaller dataset loads into the same open list — after the swap, no item can be highlighted or selected in a production build.

**Fix:** In `unregister`, reset `controlledRef.current = null` when `map.size` drops to 0. Genuine mixing within one population still errors; a wholesale swap re-derives the mode.

### 2. 🟡 `syncRefs` replaces the `elementsRef` array, dropping the externally maintained `listRef` length for partially rendered lists

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:65`

```tsx
elementsRef.current = [];
...
nextIndexRef.current = elementsRef.current.length;
```

`AriaCombobox` maintains an invariant on the same array: `listRef.current.length = flatFilteredItems.length` (`AriaCombobox.tsx:841`), but its effect only re-runs when `flatFilteredItems` changes. Previously, explicit-`index` items never registered, so `CompositeList` never touched the array after mount and the length stuck. Now every register/unregister flush replaces the array with one whose length is `maxRegisteredIndex + 1`. For a non-virtualized combobox with `items` that renders only a window of indexed items (the configuration `index` exists for, minus the `virtualized` flag — with `virtualized`, `ComboboxList` renders no `CompositeList` and this path is bypassed), moving the window re-registers items and shrinks `listRef.current.length` from the total item count to the window bound, clamping `useListNavigation`'s range.

**Failure scenario:** A combobox with 1,000 filtered items renders indexed items 0–20 without `virtualized`; after any window change, ArrowDown navigation is bounded at the last rendered index instead of index 999.

**Fix:** Mutate in place — clear and refill the existing array (or restore its prior `length` when the controlled max index is lower) instead of assigning a fresh array, matching the old identity-preserving behavior.

### 3. ℹ️ Duplicate controlled indexes silently collide

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:70`

```tsx
nextMap.forEach((metadata, node) => {
  if (metadata.index != null && metadata.index > -1) {
    elementsRef.current[metadata.index] = node;
```

Two items registering the same `index` (an easy off-by-one in user mapping code) last-write-wins in `elementsRef`, and both items report `highlighted` for the same `activeIndex`, plus a duplicate DOM `id` from `${rootId}-${index}`. The PR adds a dev error for mixing but nothing for duplicates.

**Failure scenario:** A user maps two item groups both starting at index 0; the first group's items can never be highlighted, with no diagnostic.

**Fix:** In the flush (dev only), warn when a controlled index is seen twice.

## Tests (1)

### 1. 🟡 The "controlled lists skip DOM reorder observation" behavior is untested

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.test.tsx:287`

The PR description lists three behaviors; two are pinned (registration with explicit indexes, mixing warnings), but nothing asserts that a controlled list ignores DOM reorders — i.e. that after `list.insertBefore(...)` moves controlled items, their indexes still follow the `index` props rather than document order (mirroring the existing "updates indexes when keyed groups reorder" test, inverted). A future refactor could silently re-enable the observer for controlled lists — or break the early return — without any test failing.

**Failure scenario:** The `isControlled` early-return in the observer effect is lost in a refactor; controlled indexes get clobbered by document order and no test catches it.

**Fix:** Add a test that reorders controlled items in the DOM and asserts `elementsRef` still reflects the `index` props.

## Simplifications (0)

No findings.

## Docs (1)

### 1. ℹ️ Stale and missing JSDoc for the new controlled-index contract

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/useCompositeListItem.ts:27`

```ts
/**
 * Used to register a list item and its index (DOM position) in the `CompositeList`.
 */
```

"(DOM position)" now describes only the uncontrolled mode. The `index` parameter in `UseCompositeListItemParameters` is also undocumented, and the public `ComboboxItem.index` JSDoc ("Improves performance when specified by avoiding the need to calculate the index automatically from the DOM", `ComboboxItem.tsx:310`) doesn't mention the new all-or-nothing constraint the dev error enforces.

**Failure scenario:** A user passes `index` to only the items they consider expensive, gets a console error (or silent prod misbehavior) and finds no documented rule explaining it.

**Fix:** Update the hook JSDoc to cover controlled indexes, and add a sentence to the `index` prop docs: either all items in a list receive `index` or none do (then run `pnpm docs:api`).

## Verdict

**Approve after nits** — the redesign is correct on the main paths and well tested, but the permanent mode lock and the `elementsRef` identity change each regress an edge case the old code handled.

---

🤖 Review generated with Claude Code

# PR review

This is a well-executed rewrite of `CompositeList`'s registration/flush model so that an explicit `index` makes an item's index *controlled* while still registering it (fixing the broken pointer-hover highlighting on manually-indexed lists in issue 4657). **Nothing is merge-blocking** — no 🔴. All affected suites pass (Combobox 716, Tabs 211, Toolbar 129, Slider 368, Select 492, Menu 956, OTP 156, Accordion 113), typecheck and eslint are clean, and a dedicated core-mechanism sweep found no lost registrations, stale-ref, or ordering regressions. The residual risk is concentrated in the new `itemCount` contract and the mode latch: both are latent edge cases that fail *silently* rather than loudly, plus a handful of test/doc gaps.

## Bugs (4)

### 1. 🟡 `itemCount` is gated on `hasItems`, so an externally-filtered virtualized list can't navigate past the rendered window

**Location:** `packages/react/src/combobox/list/ComboboxList.tsx:127`, `packages/react/src/combobox/root/AriaCombobox.tsx:177`

```tsx
itemCount={hasItems ? flatFilteredItems.length : undefined}   // hasItems = items !== undefined
```

The deleted `AriaCombobox` line `listRef.current.length = flatFilteredItems.length` ran regardless of the `items` prop. Its replacement, `itemCount`, is only fed when `items` is passed. When `itemCount == null`, `syncRefs` lets `elementsRef.current.length` collapse to `highestRenderedIndex + 1` instead of the logical total.

**Failure scenario:** a virtualized combobox that drives its window from `filteredItems` via external `useFilter()` **without** also passing `items` renders logical indices 900–910 with controlled `index` props; `store.state.listRef.current.length` becomes ~911 instead of 1000, and `useListNavigation`'s `getMaxListIndex`/`listRef.current.length` reads make Home/End and arrow-past-window unreachable. The `filteredItems` prop is documented to be used *alongside* `items` (in which case this is fine), so this only bites the `filteredItems`-without-`items` config — but the implicit gate deserves a deliberate decision or a comment rather than silently depending on that combination.

**Fix:** derive `itemCount` from the total filtered length whenever the list is virtualized/windowed (not only when `items` is set), or document + assert that controlled-index windowing requires `items`.

### 2. 🟡 The controlled/uncontrolled mode is latched for the list's lifetime and the mixing guard is a prod no-op

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:36`

```js
if (controlledRef.current === null) {
  controlledRef.current = isControlled;
} else if (controlledRef.current !== isControlled) {
  error(`A CompositeList is mixing controlled and uncontrolled indexes.` /* … */);
}
```

`controlledRef` is fixed to the first-registered item and never reset; `error()` is a no-op under `NODE_ENV === 'production'`. Because `ComboboxList` now wraps children in one persistent `CompositeList` (the old `if (virtualized) return element` early-return is gone), the instance survives a runtime mode switch.

**Failure scenario:** start a combobox non-virtualized (`controlledRef = false`), then toggle `virtualized` at runtime. Items remount and re-register as controlled, but the latch stays `false`, the dev error doesn't fire in prod, and `sortMap(map, false)` re-derives indexes by document position — discarding the intended filtered indexes so navigation/selection targets the wrong element. Same corruption on an empty→refill with the opposite mode. `virtualized` is documented as stable-per-instance, so this is edge/unsupported — but it degrades silently. Consider resetting the latch when the list empties, or keeping the mixing check outside the prod-stripped path for this specific corruption. Relatedly, the message names the internal `CompositeList`, which an app author using `Combobox.Item` can't act on — naming the consumer component would make it diagnosable.

### 3. 🟡 `itemCount` going number→`undefined` never shrinks `elementsRef.length` back

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:111-121`

```js
if (itemCount == null) {
  return;                          // ← bails before un-applying a previous length
}
if (elementsRef.current.length !== itemCount) {
  elementsRef.current.length = itemCount;
}
```

The standalone `itemCount` effect early-returns on `null`, and the flush effect (`[mapTick, flush]`, gated on `isDirtyRef`) doesn't run without a registration change. So if `itemCount` transitions `5 → undefined` in a commit with no mount/unmount, `elementsRef.current.length` stays `5` with phantom empty slots. Number→number transitions are handled; only →`undefined` leaks. Self-corrects on the next registration-triggered flush, and unlikely in current Combobox usage, but it's a real asymmetry in the new feature.

### 4. ℹ️ Duplicate/out-of-range controlled indexes silently drop an element

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:70-83`

`syncRefs` does `elementsRef.current[metadata.index] = node` with no collision detection (last-write-wins), then `elementsRef.current.length = itemCount` truncates any placement at or beyond `itemCount`. Two items with the same `index` prop, or an `index >= itemCount`, drop an element from `elementsRef` with no warning — navigation to that slot reaches only one (or none). Benign for Combobox (`indexFromFilter < itemCount`, indices unique), but a footgun for future controlled consumers; a dev warning on collision would mirror the existing mixing check.

## Tests (5)

### 1. 🟡 The `itemCount` dynamic-change effect is untested

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.test.tsx` — no test passes `itemCount`

No `CompositeList` unit test passes `itemCount`; the only coverage is one combobox integration test with a *static* window. The effect that trims/grows `elementsRef`/`labelsRef` length when `itemCount` changes without a registration change (the exact case its comment cites, and findings 1/3 above) is entirely uncovered — a regression there would leave navigation reaching stale indices with nothing failing.

### 2. 🟡 The hover test doesn't isolate the controlled-index path

**Location:** `packages/react/src/combobox/root/ComboboxRoot.test.tsx:1109`

Items render with `index={index}` where `index` is the natural map order, so the manual indices coincide with DOM order. The test passes even if the `index` prop were ignored — it proves the code path doesn't crash, not that the supplied index drives highlighting/`aria-activedescendant`. Reversed or non-contiguous indices would make it a real pin (and directly regression-guard the issue this PR fixes).

### 3. 🟡 Controlled-index collision is untested and undetected

Two items with the same `index` (bug 4 above) silently drop one from `elementsRef` with no assertion or warning anywhere.

### 4. 🟡 Controlled-item label change is untested

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.test.tsx:500`

"updates labels without re-registering" uses an *uncontrolled* item. For a controlled item the register deps exclude `label`, so the update rides entirely on the `ref` callback's optimistic `labelsRef.current[index]` write — a distinct path with no coverage; a stale `labelsRef` entry (broken typeahead) wouldn't be caught.

### 5. ℹ️ Smaller gaps

**Location:** `packages/react/src/internals/composite/list/CompositeList.tsx:20`


`controlledRef` is permanently fixed by the first item ever registered to that `CompositeList`. Mode mismatches only produce an error in development; production continues using the original mode.

That breaks valid runtime updates where all items change together:

- Controlled → uncontrolled: `sortMap` still takes the controlled branch, but the new metadata has no index. `syncRefs` skips every entry, leaving `elementsRef` empty or containing only `itemCount` holes.
- Uncontrolled → controlled: `sortMap` still takes the uncontrolled branch and overwrites every supplied index with DOM order.

**Failure scenario:** The public `virtualized` prop can trigger exactly this transition. `Combobox.Item` remounts when the root changes virtualization mode, but the surrounding `CompositeList` remains mounted, so its sticky mode survives.

**Fix:** Derive the mode from the currently registered map during each flush, while still warning if the current entries are mixed. Alternatively, reset it once the map becomes empty. Add controlled→uncontrolled and uncontrolled→controlled tests, including a `virtualized` toggle.

### 2. 🔴 Keep the DOM and value registries aligned with controlled indexes

**Location:** `packages/react/src/combobox/root/AriaCombobox.tsx:501`

```tsx

```

The new test deliberately supplies reverse indexes:

```tsx

banana -> 1
cherry -> 0
```

It then verifies that keyboard navigation follows that controlled order and initially highlights `cherry`. That establishes that explicit indexes are intended to control semantic ordering, not merely duplicate the existing array index.

But when `items` is provided, `valuesRef` remains in `flatFilteredItems` order:

while `listRef` becomes:

**Failure scenario:** `setIndices({ activeIndex: 0 })` visually highlights `cherry`, but immediately reports `valuesRef.current[0]`, which is `apple`, through `onItemHighlighted`. Initial selected-index resolution has the same mismatch: selected `apple` resolves to index `0`, which now points at the `cherry` element.

**Fix:** Either make `valuesRef`, selected-index resolution, and related registries controlled-index aware; or define that `index` must exactly equal the item's filtered data index, document that restriction, and stop testing reversed indexes. The current halfway state gives incorrect callbacks and incorrect initial highlighting.

### 3. 🔴 Populate the complete value registry for filteredItems-only virtualization

**Location:** `packages/react/src/combobox/root/AriaCombobox.tsx:838`

```tsx
useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
```

The latest test adds support for:

but only verifies that `listRef.length === 5`.

`CompositeList` now exposes the complete logical length, including unmounted slots. But `valuesRef` is populated from the complete filtered array only when `items` exists.
